quotes.text:
My read is that "Express Chat" is effectively a push-to-talk feature.  It's implemented as an Android and iOS app:  <https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.moon.express_chat&hl=en-US> (Android) and <https://apps.apple.com/in/app/express-chat/id6745220803> (iOS).

Several carriers offer this, usually aimed at corporate users (construction, maintenance, fleet workers, emergency responders).  See Kyocera and Sonim, particularly their rugged phone offerings (Dura from Kyocera, XP from Sonim).

Carrier-based PTT is typically limited only to other phonesets on that carrier, though in practice the feature is generally accessed through a programmable key, and can be configured to use another (unlimited) press-to-talk app, such as Zello (which I've seen before) or Express Chat (#TIL).

My guess is because this is not an Android phone and it is important to be able to chat with Android and iPhone users. The real question is why would iPhone and Android users install this app?

https://www.hmd.com/en_in/about-hybrid-phones

Edit: Requiring Google Play login to use this express chat app is pretty stupid in my opinion. Why do apps require Google Play login? Especially a Chinese app? I am on an Android phone with Google play. I am just not signed in to Google play. I installed this app with Aurora store. The app simply throws me back to Play Store which tells me to sign in. Why?
